Subject: Residency / SCCs and UK Addendum compatibility question

Marissa —

Thanks for taking this. Procurement and legal have a couple of interlocking asks before we can progress to DocuSign:

- Confirmation that Redwood can sign standard EU SCCs and the UK IDTA (or a UK Addendum) and whether execution will be on our contract or via a separately executed attachment.
- Can you provide a TIA/DTIA mapping that shows where tokenization, KV cache, and telemetry logs may leave the EU, and any technical/organizational safeguards? Our data residency requirement is EU-only processing for patient data; we need evidence for that.
- Complete subprocessor list and the latest attestations (SOC2+subprocessor access controls).

Procurement will also need an estimated artifact delivery timeline (we're on a hard quarter close). If you can send a short checklist and sample artifacts we can review that will speed approval.

We'd prefer a 2-week turn for artifacts; is that feasible?

Cheers,
Tom

Tom — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, details and artifacts attached: redwood_safeguards_matrix.xlsx and an initial DDQ extract.

- Execution: We can execute the EU SCCs and the UK IDTA (UK Addendum) either appended to your DPA or as an executed schedule; legal usually prefers a single DocuSign envelope for SCCs + Addendum.
- TIA/DTIA mapping: we can provide a technical transfer impact assessment that maps processing stages (ingest, KV cache, model runtime, telemetry). Note: our serving runtime supports region pinning and we can configure strict EU-only model routing for customer accounts; however some operational telemetry (health checks, anonymized metrics) may transit non-EU endpoints unless explicitly suppressed — see matrix.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a current subprocessor registry; we can provide attestations for critical subprocessors and a CSV export.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the precise EU region(s) for processing (e.g., eu-west-1 / eu-central-1).
2) We'll start an artifacts sprint: 10 business days to deliver the full TIA mapping, subprocessor CSV, and SOC2 excerpts.
3) Kimberly / Jonas, can you confirm the telemetry suppression options and whether we can provide an auditable log redaction snapshot for Medialife?

If that timeline works Tom, I can generate a DocuSign envelope with SCCs + UK Addendum placeholders after we confirm PO/contract path.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance

Marissa / Kimberly —

Short answers from infra/serving runtime perspective:
- Region pinning: We support account-level routing policies that pin inference and KV cache to EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1). When enabled, model runtime and KV cache remain in-region.
- Telemetry: Application-level telemetry (traces, anonymized metrics) can be configured to stay in-region, but platform-level health probes and some provider-level metrics may still be collected outside the EU during cross-region failover windows. We can provide a suppression profile and a redaction snapshot for audit.
- TIA/DTIA artifacts: We can produce a mapping file and sequence diagram that shows data flow; estimate: 8 business days to assemble initial mapping + controls matrix if we get the exact region(s) and the tenant config. Full substantiation (logs + attestations) ~12 business days.
- KMS/HSM: Keys are customer-specific; we support customer-managed KMS in EU regions and can provide key location notes for the TIA.

I'll start the mapping once Marissa confirms region(s) and scope.

— Jonas
